title: Feedback factor (feedback 0.8)
purpose: Exercises the `feedback` factor of the `epsr` engine [@soper1996,@soper2005]: the confidence placed in the data when the empirical potential is derived, entering the inversion of the neutron weights matrix. Changing it from the value stored with the run forces the inverse weights to be recalculated, a code path not taken by the base case.
fortran: `epsr_standalone_rev3.f`: `ptgnsq` (EP refinement with the new inverse weights), `runepsr17`
system: The EPSR-test system: a liquid mixture of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO, (CH3)2SO) and 400 water molecules (DMSO mole fraction 1/3; 3200 atoms) at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å (atomic number density 0.0881 atoms/Å³). DMSO uses EPSR's Lennard-Jones + Coulomb reference potential with methyl rotational groups; water uses SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charge parameters [@berendsen1987] with EPSR's flexible intramolecular geometry (O-H 0.976 Å). The empirical potential is refined against three neutron diffraction data sets of deuterated DMSO in D2O, in null-scattering H2O/D2O and in H2O (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), the isotope-substitution approach of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. With `feedback` f the structure factors used to update the EP are formed from a fraction f of the data and 1 - f of the simulation; f is lowered from 0.9 to 0.8.
inputs: Copy of EPSR-test with only `feedback 0.8` (instead of 0.9) in `200DMSO400Water.EPSR.inp`.
verification: Two chained passes: in pass 1 `get_wts` compares the new factor with the value stored in the `.inpa` accumulator file (`feedbackold` 0.9) and rebuilds the inverse weights matrix; the `.inpa` written then holds 0.8, so pass 2 reuses the stored inverse. The written `.inp` keeps `feedback 0.8`. All 27 output files, including `.pcof` with the refined EP coefficients and `delfit.dat`, are identical after both passes, which requires the same double-precision matrix inversion and the same order of `ran1` draws.
